newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Illiterate millionaires in South Trinidad.
newsitem.headline: Illiterate millionaires in South Trinidad.

text.p: Trinidad and Tobago has at least 30 Indian millionaires who are illiterate, according to Sat Maharaj, secretary general of the Sanatan Dharma Maha Sabha, the largest Indian organisation in the two-island state.

Addressing a banking conference on Saturday at the organisation's headquarters, he told the meeting attended by leading figures in the banking industry that the affluent Indians cannot even sign their names.
Instead they used thumbprints to do business, he said.
Most of these wealthly Trinidadians live in the southern districts of Debe and Penal.

"If you go down to Debe and Penal (agricultural areas), there are people who own million of dollars in fixed deposits and cannot sign their names. They put an X or thumb print but they own millions," he said.
Indians of Hindu faith hold the most fixed deposits at banks in the two-island state with deposits, according to Maharaj, with over $25 million.
Maharaj chaired the one-day meeting, which was attended also by Prime Minister Basdeo Panday and Sir Neville Nicholas, chairman of the Barbados-based Caribbean Development Bank.

Panday told the meeting: "The government and the Central Bank are concerned primarily with the stability of the country's financial system and we are prepared to take such action as required to promote that stability."
His statement came in the wake of further erosion of the Trinidad and Tobago dollar. On Sept. 24 the currency was devalued by one percent. Last week it suffered a further fall.
Finance Minister Brian Kuei Tung said: "I am confident the situation will stabilise in the near future."
